proposed_bom.purpose: 3 baseline instances (one per AZ) x 730 h + 7 extra for 60 peak hours

justification: The original web tier tops out at 160 requests per second. The redesign spreads t3.small instances (80 requests per second each) across three Availability Zones with a minimum of three and a maximum of twelve, so ten instances meet the 750 requests per second origin peak; database load is handled by a larger db.r6g.large instead of a cache. Operational excellence: the stack is defined in CloudFormation and scaling is automatic. Security: instances stay in private subnets behind the load balancer and use a scoped instance role. Reliability: three Availability Zones keep at least two instances running after an AZ loss, and a Multi-AZ db.r6g.large with 14-day backups and point-in-time recovery meets the RPO and RTO. Performance efficiency: many small instances let target tracking add capacity in fine steps, and the memory-optimised database removes the need for ElastiCache. Cost optimisation: about US$705 per month, within the US$750 budget; burst instances are paid only during peaks. Sustainability: fine-grained scaling keeps utilisation high and idle capacity low.
comparison: The original costs US$133.21 and cannot reach the peak; the proposal costs US$704.60 and spans three Availability Zones.
